title: Meridian Pay A2A, one hop at a time: a delegated token chain you walk yourself

glossary.definition: One leg of a delegated call: a token crosses from one actor to the next, usually through a token exchange. The demo walks the hops one at a time, by hand, so each change is visible.

RFC 8693. An OAuth grant where one token is swapped for another at the authorization server: the caller presents a subject_token (and optionally an actor_token) and receives a new access token with a different audience, scope, or act claim.

An object-valued claim in an access token naming the actor that is acting for the subject (RFC 8693). act.sub is the agent; sub is the person or workload it acts for. Nested act claims build the chain.

A JWT signed by an issuer outside the platform's own trust domain (a platform-issued agent identity, a SPIFFE workload). The platform establishes trust in that issuer once - issuer string plus JWKS - and then accepts its tokens as subject or actor in a token exchange.

The optional second token in an RFC 8693 request. It names who is doing the exchanging. For a third-party actor it must carry type urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt; PingOne refuses access_token for it.
The agent that faces the person. It holds the person's token, decides which specialist handles the request, and exchanges the person's token for one scoped to that specialist.
A scoped agent that owns one capability (payouts, payments). Each has its own resource, audience, MCP door, and tool policy. A specialist's token must not open another specialist's door.

A Privilege-registered MCP endpoint with its own required claims (act.sub, client_id) and audience. The gateway refuses a call whose token does not satisfy the door's claims, even if the signature is valid.
The full sequence of tokens a request accumulated, read side by side: who the subject was at each hop and who acted for them. The demo's Captured Tokens panel is this chain, live.
